# dgees

> Computes the eigenvalues, the Schur form, and, optionally, the matrix of Schur vectors for general matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgees from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgees';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgees(
    order,
    jobvs, sort,
    select,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    sdim,
    WR, strideWR,
    WI, strideWI,
    VS, LDVS,
    WORK,
    BWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobvs` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'no-vectors'`: Schur vectors are not computed; `'compute-vectors'`: Schur vectors are computed. |
| `sort` | `("none"\|"sort")` | in |  | one of `'none'`, `'sort'` | specifies whether or not to order the eigenvalues on the diagonal of the Schur form. `'none'`: Eigenvalues are not ordered; `'sort'`: Eigenvalues are ordered (see SELECT). |
| `select` | `Function` | in |  |  | sELECT must be declared EXTERNAL in the calling subroutine. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | the order of the matrix A. |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | on entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten by its real Schur form T. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `sdim` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | if `sort === 'none'`, SDIM = 0. |
| `WR` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | wR and WI contain the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues in the same order that they appear on the diagonal of the output Schur form T. |
| ↳ `strideWR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WR` |
| `WI` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | wR and WI contain the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues in the same order that they appear on the diagonal of the output Schur form T. |
| ↳ `strideWI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WI` |
| `VS` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × N` |  | if `jobvs === 'compute-vectors'`, VS contains the orthogonal matrix Z of Schur vectors. |
| ↳ `LDVS` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldvs < 1 \|\| (jobvs === 'compute-vectors' && ldvs < N)` | leading dimension of `VS` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ MINWRK` |  | workspace of at least `max(1,3*N)` elements, or `null` to allocate the reference's optimum (MAXWRK, with the callees' optima, NB from `ilaenv`: dgehrd `N*NB + 4160`, dorghr `(N-1)*NB` with Schur vectors, and dhseqr's LWKOPT) |
| `BWORK` | `(Uint8Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `N` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvs`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Schur vectors are not computed;
  -   `= 'V'`: Schur vectors are computed.
- `sort`: Specifies whether or not to order the eigenvalues on the diagonal of the Schur form.

  -   `= 'N'`: Eigenvalues are not ordered;
  -   `= 'S'`: Eigenvalues are ordered (see `SELECT`).
- `select`: `SELECT` must be declared EXTERNAL in the calling subroutine. If `SORT = 'S'`, `SELECT` is used to select eigenvalues to sort to the top left of the Schur form. If `SORT = 'N'`, `SELECT` is not referenced. An eigenvalue $\mathrm{WR}(j)+\sqrt{-1} \, \mathrm{WI}(j)$ is selected if `SELECT(WR(j),WI(j))` is true; i.e., if either one of a complex conjugate pair of eigenvalues is selected, then both complex eigenvalues are selected. Note that a selected complex eigenvalue may no longer satisfy `SELECT(WR(j),WI(j))` = .TRUE. after ordering, since ordering may change the value of complex eigenvalues (especially if the eigenvalue is ill-conditioned); in this case `INFO` is set to N+2 (see `INFO` below).
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten by its real Schur form T.
- `sdim`: If `SORT = 'N'`, `SDIM = 0`. If `SORT = 'S'`, `SDIM` = number of eigenvalues (after sorting)

  -   for which `SELECT` is true. (Complex conjugate
  -   pairs for which `SELECT` is true for either
  -   eigenvalue count as 2.)
- `WI`: `WR` and `WI` contain the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues in the same order that they appear on the diagonal of the output Schur form T. Complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues will appear consecutively with the eigenvalue having the positive imaginary part first.
- `VS`: If `JOBVS = 'V'`, `VS` contains the orthogonal matrix Z of Schur vectors. If `JOBVS = 'N'`, `VS` is not referenced.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` contains the optimal `LWORK`.
- `BWORK`: Not referenced if `SORT = 'N'`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "none", "sort"
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVS < 1 \|\| ( jobvs === "compute-vectors" && LDVS < N )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgees.ndarray(
    jobvs, sort,
    select,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    sdim,
    WR, strideWR, offsetWR,
    WI, strideWI, offsetWI,
    VS, strideVS1, strideVS2, offsetVS,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    BWORK, strideBWork, offsetBWork
) → integer
```

Computes for an N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrix A, the eigenvalues, the real.
Schur form T, and, optionally, the matrix of Schur vectors Z. This gives
the Schur factorization A = Z_T_Z**T.

Optionally, it also orders the eigenvalues on the diagonal of the real Schur
form so that selected eigenvalues are at the top left. The leading columns
of Z then form an orthonormal basis for the invariant subspace corresponding
to the selected eigenvalues.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobvs` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'none'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `sort` | `("none"\|"sort")` | in |  | one of `'none'`, `'sort'` | `'none'` or `'sort'` |
| `select` | `Function` | in |  |  | function(wr, wi) returning boolean; used when sort=`'sort'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | N-by-N matrix, overwritten with Schur form T on exit |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for A |
| `sdim` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output: sdim[0] = number of eigenvalues for which SELECT is true |
| `WR` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: real parts of eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideWR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WR |
| ↳ `offsetWR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WR |
| `WI` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: imaginary parts of eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideWI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WI |
| ↳ `offsetWI` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WI |
| `VS` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × N` |  | output: N-by-N matrix of Schur vectors |
| ↳ `strideVS1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of VS |
| ↳ `strideVS2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of VS |
| ↳ `offsetVS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for VS |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ MINWRK` |  | workspace of at least `max(1,3*N)` elements (the reference's minimum); for good performance, the optimum MAXWRK the wrapper allocates for `null` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK |
| `BWORK` | `Uint8Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | boolean workspace of length N (used when sort=`'sort'`) |
| ↳ `strideBWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BWORK |
| ↳ `offsetBWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for BWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvs`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Schur vectors are not computed;
  -   `= 'V'`: Schur vectors are computed.
- `sort`: Specifies whether or not to order the eigenvalues on the diagonal of the Schur form.

  -   `= 'N'`: Eigenvalues are not ordered;
  -   `= 'S'`: Eigenvalues are ordered (see `SELECT`).
- `select`: `SELECT` must be declared EXTERNAL in the calling subroutine. If `SORT = 'S'`, `SELECT` is used to select eigenvalues to sort to the top left of the Schur form. If `SORT = 'N'`, `SELECT` is not referenced. An eigenvalue $\mathrm{WR}(j)+\sqrt{-1} \, \mathrm{WI}(j)$ is selected if `SELECT(WR(j),WI(j))` is true; i.e., if either one of a complex conjugate pair of eigenvalues is selected, then both complex eigenvalues are selected. Note that a selected complex eigenvalue may no longer satisfy `SELECT(WR(j),WI(j))` = .TRUE. after ordering, since ordering may change the value of complex eigenvalues (especially if the eigenvalue is ill-conditioned); in this case `INFO` is set to N+2 (see `INFO` below).
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten by its real Schur form T.
- `sdim`: If `SORT = 'N'`, `SDIM = 0`. If `SORT = 'S'`, `SDIM` = number of eigenvalues (after sorting)

  -   for which `SELECT` is true. (Complex conjugate
  -   pairs for which `SELECT` is true for either
  -   eigenvalue count as 2.)
- `WI`: `WR` and `WI` contain the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues in the same order that they appear on the diagonal of the output Schur form T. Complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues will appear consecutively with the eigenvalue having the positive imaginary part first.
- `VS`: If `JOBVS = 'V'`, `VS` contains the orthogonal matrix Z of Schur vectors. If `JOBVS = 'N'`, `VS` is not referenced.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` contains the optimal `LWORK`.
- `BWORK`: Not referenced if `SORT = 'N'`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info (0=success, >0 eigenvalue computation failed, N+1/N+2 sorting issues)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "none", "sort"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option
- `RangeError` `BWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetBWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is \<= N: the QR algorithm failed to compute all the eigenvalues; elements 1:ILO-1 and i+1:N of `WR` and `WI` contain those eigenvalues which have converged; if `JOBVS = 'V'`, `VS` contains the matrix which reduces A to its partially converged Schur form. = N+1: the eigenvalues could not be reordered because some eigenvalues were too close to separate (the problem is very ill-conditioned); = N+2: after reordering, roundoff changed values of some complex eigenvalues so that leading eigenvalues in the Schur form no longer satisfy `SELECT`=.TRUE.  This could also be caused by underflow due to scaling.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Uint8Array from '@stdlib/array/uint8/lib/index.js';
import dgees from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgees';

/**
* Selects eigenvalues with a positive real part.
*
* @private
* @param {number} wr - real part of the eigenvalue
* @param {number} wi - imaginary part of the eigenvalue
* @returns {boolean} boolean indicating whether to select the eigenvalue
*/
function select( wr, wi ) { // eslint-disable-line no-unused-vars
	return wr > 0.0;
}

// Real Schur factorization A = Z * T * Z^T of a 3x3 matrix (column-major), sorting eigenvalues with positive real part first:
const N = 3;
const sdim = new Int32Array( 1 );

// Using the standard interface:
let A = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 3.0, 0.0, -2.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, -4.0 ] );
let WR = new Float64Array( N );
let WI = new Float64Array( N );
let VS = new Float64Array( N * N );
let info = dgees( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'sort', select, N, A, N, sdim, WR, 1, WI, 1, VS, N, null, null );
console.log( info, sdim[ 0 ], WR, WI ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 3.0, 0.0, -2.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, -4.0 ] );
WR = new Float64Array( N );
WI = new Float64Array( N );
VS = new Float64Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 3 * N );
const BWORK = new Uint8Array( N );
info = dgees.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'sort', select, N, A, 1, N, 0, sdim, WR, 1, 0, WI, 1, 0, VS, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0, BWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, sdim[ 0 ], WR, WI ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGEES`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGEES computes for an N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrix A, the eigenvalues, the real Schur form T, and, optionally, the matrix of Schur vectors Z. This gives the Schur factorization $A = Z \, T \, (Z^T)$.

Optionally, it also orders the eigenvalues on the diagonal of the real Schur form so that selected eigenvalues are at the top left. The leading columns of Z then form an orthonormal basis for the invariant subspace corresponding to the selected eigenvalues.

A matrix is in real Schur form if it is upper quasi-triangular with 1-by-1 and 2-by-2 blocks. 2-by-2 blocks will be standardized in the form

$$
\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & a \end{bmatrix}
$$

where $b \, c < 0$. The eigenvalues of such a block are a +- sqrt(bc).

</section>
